subject: Question: data access & subprocessors in DPA for Acme (needs Product/Security input)
messages:
From: Sara Clark <sara.clark@acme.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acme-corp.com, procure@acme.com
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: DPA addendum questions (subprocessors + analytics access)

Hi Dev,

Thanks for sending the DPA addendum. Legal flagged two items that need internal input before we can sign: the subprocessor notification & the clause that permits Redwood to use aggregated telemetry for product analytics. High level:

- Acme procurement is asking whether we can get advance notice + 10 business days to object to new subprocessors that would have access to customer data.
- Their legal team is uncomfortable with opaque "product analytics" language — they want a narrow definition and assurances that PII won't be used for model training.

I've attached their latest mark-up and the subprocessor list they pulled from the vendor portal. Can Product and Security confirm whether the request is feasible, or if we can offer specific language (e.g., notification + right to object for high-risk subprocessors only)?

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Clark
Head of Procurement, Acme Corporation

Attachments: Acme_DPA_Addendum_v3.pdf, subprocessor_list_2026-04-15.csv

From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: Sara Clark <sara.clark@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA addendum questions (subprocessors + analytics access)

Sara — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Looping in Marissa (legal liaison), Hannah (Security), and Laura (Product) to scope answers. Quick notes from me:

- We typically provide notification of new subprocessors and a short objection window, but 10 business days is slightly longer than our standard 5 business days for low/medium-risk subs.
- For high-risk subprocessors (e.g., storage or logging providers that could access plaintext data), we can offer notification + 10 business days on a case-by-case basis.
- Regarding analytics: our telemetry pipeline collects aggregated metrics (latency, token counts, feature flags) and we maintain a strict aggregation and PII-filtering layer; we do not train models on customer-provided plaintext.

Marissa/Hannah/Laura — what specific wording can we propose that keeps us operationally flexible but addresses their ask? Also: is there a straightforward way for Product to enumerate what counts as "high-risk"?

— Dev
Engineering Manager, Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: dev_patel@redwood.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA addendum questions (subprocessors + analytics access)

Folks — I reviewed Acme's mark-up. Operationally acceptable compromise I can propose:

1) Subprocessor notice: Redwood will provide written notice of any new subprocessor additions and allow a 5 business day review period. For subprocessors that will have access to unencrypted customer data or telemetry labeled as customer-content, Redwood will provide a 10 business day notice and will engage in good-faith discussions if Acme objects.

2) Analytics / data use: Add a definition: "Aggregated telemetry" means data aggregated across customers such that individual customer data cannot be isolated, and no plaintext customer-provided content is used for model training. Add an explicit statement: "Redwood will not use customer-provided plaintext for model training without explicit written consent."

If Security is comfortable with the "high-risk" definition (see Hannah), I think that language is defensible. Marissa

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA addendum questions (subprocessors + analytics access)

Thanks Marissa — I agree in principle but want to tighten a couple of points from a security posture perspective:

- Define "access to unencrypted customer data" precisely: systems where operators or subprocessors can retrieve customer content in plaintext (examples: logging pipeline with plaintext logs, backup restores, third-party support tools).
- For the 10 business day window: Security needs a written process for emergency quick-add (e.g., critical vulnerability requiring immediate rotation to a new vendor). If we keep a 10-business-day objection window, we should add a carve-out: Redwood may add a subprocessor immediately for security or safety reasons, provided we notify the customer within 24 hours and provide remediation plans.
- Telemetry pipeline: I'm attaching the brief (internal) diagram of our telemetry filter that shows PII scrubbing and aggregation thresholds. If Product confirms the thresholds line up with the proposed "aggregated" definition, Security is comfortable with the training prohibition clause.

I'll attach the telemetry diagram and propose a short clause for the emergency subprocessor path.

— Hannah
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: telemetry_pipeline_summary.png

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA addendum questions (subprocessors + analytics access)

Thanks team — quick Product input and the action items I can own: 

- Definition: Product confirms that "aggregated telemetry" for contractual purposes = metrics that are rolled up to cohorts of >=100 distinct customers or otherwise processed so individual customer sequences cannot be reconstructed. We'll add that as explicit wording.
- Training: We will include the explicit prohibition on using plaintext customer content for model training without written consent.
- High-risk subprocessors: Product and Security agree the examples Hannah listed (logging with plaintext, backup restores, human-in-the-loop support tools) count as high-risk. We'll provide the operational checklist to identify high-risk candidates within 3 business days.

Action items (I will):
1) Draft the proposed replacement clauses (subprocessor notice with 5/10 day split, emergency carve-out, analytics definition, training prohibition).
2) Put the checklist in Confluence and share the link with Legal & Security (https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/Telemetry+and+Subprocessors).
3) Send a short note to Acme with the draft language and ask if that addresses their concerns.

If no objections from Legal/Security by EOD tomorrow, I'll send the draft to Sara.

— Laura
Product Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference
